story.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says

facts.text: Meta employees have raised concerns that the company’s AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data, according to a new Reuters report that looked at internal company posts.

“Employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products,” a Meta spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”
Launched in September, Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps on record, with more than 10 million downloads.

One employee told colleagues that Muse had randomly sent an extra message in a chat about weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”
Update 11/19/2026 12:05 PM PT: The article was updated to include Meta’s comment.

In some of these instances, employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn’t belong to them.

Meta launched its Muse AI agent in September 2026 with a promise that it was built from the ground up for privacy and security, but Reuters reviewed internal communications showing employees raising “significant concerns” about Muse’s handling of private data.

Reuters reported that internal posts described incidents where Muse appeared to be mixing up conversations between different user accounts, and employees flagged safety issues “as recently as launch week” while Meta proceeded with the September 2026 US launch as scheduled.
Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests employees said they never made and bank account balances that did not belong to them.

Muse had already been downloaded by more than 10 million people and Meta expected it to generate billions of dollars in revenue from AI, while La Nación described internal postings reviewed by Reuters as showing unsolicited actions including infiltrating encrypted personal messages and sending conversations that appeared destined for other people.
This article is an automated aggregation of coverage from news outlets.
Our editorials offer in-depth analysis curated by the NewsCord team.
5 outlets in this story. Read their headlines below .

Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts told TechCrunch that “employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public,” and Roberts described Reuters’ examples as “isolated incidents.” Ars Technica quoted a Meta staffer writing “Hmmm,” after Muse sent the definition of “money laundering” unbidden, and Ars Technica also quoted the staffer’s out-of-context output about a coffee table pickup that “doesn’t seem to be yours.”
Meta Muse reportedly mixes conversations from different accounts, exposing private data.
Internal testing flagged Muse accessing encrypted private messages users did not expect.
Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show

Claroc discovered that Muse’s chat-sharing feature exposed shared conversations through publicly searchable DNS records, and Claroc found that users who shared a conversation did not realize the resulting links were discoverable by anyone with the right DNS query.

Meta launched its Muse AI agent with a promise that it was built from the ground up for privacy and security.A recent investigation and several reports reveal that the people testing the product internally were raising serious doubts about whether that promise was being met before and even after the product shipped.Meta Employees Expose Muse AI Privacy ConcernsReuters reviewed internal communications at Meta that showed employees raising significant concerns about Muse's handling of private data, including incidents where the AI agent appeared to be mixing up conversations between different user accounts.

Meta did not dispute that the internal posts existed.Separately, security firm Claroc discovered that the chat-sharing feature in Muse exposed shared conversations through publicly searchable DNS records.

Security researchers needed a single DNS query to surface thousands of previously shared chat links, all of which were accessible to anyone who found them, without any login requirement.The exposed conversations were created by users who had explicitly chosen to share them with specific recipients but did not expect that those links would be discoverable by third parties.

Meta is one of the most widely used technology companies in the world, with billions of users across its apps, and it generates revenue primarily through advertising across its social media platforms.What Is Meta Muse?Meta Muse is an AI agent developed by Meta and launched for US users in September 2026.

Organizations using Muse in business contexts should establish clear internal policies about which categories of information employees may submit to AI assistants and audit which tools are connected to business accounts.

passages: Meta launched its Muse AI agent with a promise that it was built from the ground up for privacy and security.A recent investigation and several reports reveal that the people testing the product internally were raising serious doubts about whether that promise was being met before and even after the product shipped.Meta Employees Expose Muse AI Privacy ConcernsReuters reviewed internal communications at Meta that showed employees raising significant concerns about Muse's handling of private data, including incidents where the AI agent appeared to be mixing up conversations between different user accounts.

Each Muse agent runs in its own cloud virtual machine, gated by a separate security process called Sentinel.Is Meta Muse a Security Liability?Based on the Reuters investigation, Claroc's research, and the Ars Technica reporting on internal Meta communications, Muse had experienced multiple distinct security and privacy failures by November 2026, two months after its US launch.The failures range from the DNS-accessible shared chat links, which exposed conversations that users believed were private, to internal testing that showed Muse reading Signal messages without direct user instruction, to employees reporting cross-account data confusion during testing.

Meta did not dispute that the internal posts existed.Separately, security firm Claroc discovered that the chat-sharing feature in Muse exposed shared conversations through publicly searchable DNS records.

Those internal posts revealed a pattern of safety issues that employees believed could expose private data, with some describing failure modes that made the product unreliable in real-world conditions.Employees testing Muse as recently as launch week flagged these concerns through internal channels, yet Meta proceeded with the September 2026 US launch as scheduled.

During controlled tests conducted by Reuters, Muse accessed private Signal messages on the device where it was installed, made possible by the broad Android notification permissions the app requests.Muse also sent employees unsolicited bank balance figures from an unidentified source during testing, raising concerns about where the financial data was originating from and how the agent was processing information it had not been directly prompted to retrieve.Employees also raised concerns about a human concierge feature that Meta had been developing alongside Muse.

Security researchers needed a single DNS query to surface thousands of previously shared chat links, all of which were accessible to anyone who found them, without any login requirement.The exposed conversations were created by users who had explicitly chosen to share them with specific recipients but did not expect that those links would be discoverable by third parties.

The sharing feature vulnerability was identified, reported to Meta through a bug bounty program, and patched.For users who want to minimize risk while using Muse, security researchers and IT experts recommend treating any AI agent with broad device permissions with caution, avoiding sharing conversations containing sensitive personal, financial, or business information through any AI tool's share feature, and monitoring the app's permission settings to understand what data Muse can access.

Meta is one of the most widely used technology companies in the world, with billions of users across its apps, and it generates revenue primarily through advertising across its social media platforms.What Is Meta Muse?Meta Muse is an AI agent developed by Meta and launched for US users in September 2026.
